newsitem.title: USA: Bausch & Lomb to see $0.15/shr Q4 gain.
newsitem.headline: Bausch & Lomb to see $0.15/shr Q4 gain.

text.p: Bausch & Lomb said Monday it completed the sale of its dental implant business, Steri-Oss Inc, to a group of investors sponsored by Finisterre Capital Partners, a health care investment company based in New York City, and members of Steri-Oss management.
In the fourth quarter of 1996, Bausch & Lomb said it will record a non-recurring after-tax gain of $8.5 million, or $0.15 per share, on the sale.
Additional financial details of the transaction are not being disclosed, the company said.

"The dental implant product line is not strategically linked to our core eye care businesses," said William H. Waltrip, chairman and CEO. "This sale will allow Bausch & Lomb to better concentrate its resources and attention on building our global eye care franchise, and will allow Steri-Oss to focus on growing in the specialty dental field."
Steri-Oss, which is located in Yorba Linda, Calif., is a leading manufacturer of dental implants, primarily surgical and prosthetic devices used in the replacement of missing teeth.
The buyers said the company will operate the business in its current location with the existing management team.
